five_senses_checkin.fit_notes: The universal grounding activity. Hard to get wrong. Works for almost any state except acute dysregulation where the student can't focus.
avoid_if: student is too dysregulated to focus
student is shut down and won't engage verbally

feeling_scan.fit_notes: Requires the student to sit still and turn inward. Good when they're calm enough to notice. Not for the middle of a meltdown.

sensory_stomp_shake.fit_notes: Jr only. The go-to for 'they cannot sit still'. Loud, physical, joyful. Bad fit for older students or shutdown states.
avoid_if: any setting where loud movement is inappropriate

what_keeps_me_well.fit_notes: 20-minute reflective activity. Not for an in-the-moment crisis - for proactive wellbeing time.

personal_cheerleader.fit_notes: Strong for self-esteem work. Can feel cringe if rushed or done with the wrong tone for Sr students.

positive_outlook.fit_notes: Quick, social, low-risk. Great class-warmer. Not deep work.
avoid_if: a student in real distress (this is too light)

highlight_reel.fit_notes: Useful for shifting perspective. If a student literally cannot think of anything positive, don't push - pivot.
avoid_if: student is mid-grief or major life event (can feel dismissive)

guided_imagery.fit_notes: Sr-leaning. Requires sustained focus. Excellent for anxiety if the student can settle.
avoid_if: student with trauma triggered by closing eyes / visualisation

best_for: discreet self-regulation (can be done quietly at a desk)
five_finger_breathing.fit_notes: Universal. Combines breath + tactile + focus. Excellent emergency tool.

gratitude_chain.fit_notes: Pair-share format. Quick and social. Not deep work.
avoid_if: student who is socially anxious about peer interaction in that moment

butterfly_hugs.fit_notes: Powerful nervous-system regulator using bilateral stimulation. Brief explanation important - looks unusual.
avoid_if: student who has been told to avoid self-soothing of this type for therapeutic reasons (rare)

best_for: Jr students who can't verbalise feelings
draw_it_out.fit_notes: Jr only. Externalises the emotion. Great for kids who go quiet when asked 'what's wrong'.

inner_weather_report.fit_notes: Jr only. Weather metaphor makes feelings safe to name.

best_for: students who hold stress in the body
tense_release.fit_notes: Progressive muscle relaxation. Works for any age. Needs a calm space.

sensory_scrunch.fit_notes: Tactile release. Less performative than stomp & shake - works for Sr too.
avoid_if: acute distress where the action might escalate (rare)

shape_shifting.fit_notes: Jr only. Joyful and silly. Good for releasing tension through play.
avoid_if: student feeling self-conscious about being silly

appreciation_postits.fit_notes: Sr-friendly. Takes 10 minutes but builds belonging. Specific compliments only - coach against appearance comments.
avoid_if: class with ongoing serious peer conflict (could be weaponised)
very small group where anonymity isn't possible

circle_of_safety.fit_notes: Sr. Helps students externalise who they can go to. Watch for students who can't fill it in - that's information.
avoid_if: without follow-up plan if a student reveals they have no support

tension_tamers.fit_notes: Jr. Choice of movement gives autonomy. Quick.

best_for: students who respond to visual imagery
colour_breathing.fit_notes: Universal. Adds visual element to breathwork. Calming and creative.

body_scan.fit_notes: Universal. Takes 6 min. Requires a calm-ish setting.
avoid_if: dysregulated student who can't sit still
trauma-history student where body focus is contraindicated (consult counsellor)

mindful_motion.fit_notes: Needs props or a YouTube video. Calming and passive - great when student is exhausted.

best_for: neurodivergent students who like sensory structure
mindful_listening_walk.fit_notes: Takes 10 min and needs space to walk. Great for resetting after lunch.
